chapters.n: Paul calls himself God’s servant and Christ’s apostle, sent to build up the faith of God’s chosen people and their knowledge of the truth that leads to godly living.

f.g: That leads to and fits with godly living.

chapters.n: That faith rests on the hope of eternal life, which God — who cannot lie — promised before the world began. Latter-day Saints connect this with promises made in the premortal life.
At the right time God revealed this message through preaching, which was entrusted to Paul by God’s command.

f.g: At the proper time, in God’s timing.

chapters.n: To Titus, Paul’s true son in their shared faith. Titus was a Greek convert and trusted troubleshooter in Paul’s missions.

f.g: The faith shared by all believers.

chapters.n: Paul left Titus on the island of Crete to put the young branches in order and appoint elders in every town as Paul directed.

f.g: A large island south of Greece.

chapters.n: An elder must be above reproach, faithful to his wife, with believing children who are not wild or rebellious.
As God’s steward, a bishop must be blameless: not arrogant, quick-tempered, a drunkard, violent, or greedy for dishonest gain.

f.g: Manager of a household on behalf of its owner.

chapters.n: Instead he must be hospitable, love what is good, and be sensible, fair, devout, and self-controlled.
He must hold firmly to the trustworthy message as taught, so he can encourage people with healthy doctrine and correct those who oppose it.
There are many rebellious people, empty talkers, and deceivers — especially some Jewish Christians insisting on circumcision and the law of Moses.

f.g: Those requiring Gentile converts to be circumcised.

chapters.n: They must be silenced, because they are upsetting whole families by teaching what they shouldn’t — and doing it for money.
Paul quotes a Cretan poet, Epimenides, who called his own people liars, wild beasts, and lazy gluttons. It was a well-known proverb about Crete.

f.g: Epimenides of Crete, a sixth-century BC poet considered a seer.

chapters.n: Paul agrees the description fits these false teachers, so Titus should correct them firmly so their faith becomes healthy.
They should stop paying attention to Jewish myths and human rules invented by people who reject truth.
To the pure in heart, everything is pure. But to the corrupt and unbelieving, nothing is pure — their very minds and consciences are polluted.

f.w: Unto the pure all things are pure

chapters.n: They claim to know God, but their actions deny Him. They are detestable, disobedient, and unfit for any good work.
But you, Titus, teach what fits healthy doctrine. Paul now applies good doctrine to every age and role in the branch.
Older men should be clear-minded, dignified, self-controlled, and healthy in faith, love, and endurance.
Likewise older women should live reverently, not slander others or be addicted to wine, but teach what is good.

f.g: Like people devoted to sacred service.

chapters.n: They can mentor younger women to be wise and to love their husbands and children. Paul envisions women teaching women.
Younger women should be sensible, pure, devoted to their homes, kind, and supportive of their husbands, so that no one can criticize God’s word.

f.w: that the word of God be not blasphemed
f.g: So the gospel’s reputation is protected in pagan society.

chapters.n: Encourage young men likewise to be self-controlled.
Titus himself must be an example in everything, teaching with integrity, seriousness, and sincerity.
His words should be wholesome and above criticism, so opponents will be embarrassed, having nothing bad to say.

f.w: he that is of the contrary part

chapters.n: Slaves should obey their masters, do their best to please them, and not talk back.
They should not steal, but prove fully trustworthy, so that their lives make the teaching of God our Savior attractive in every way.

f.g: Make beautiful, attractive — like arranging jewels.

chapters.n: God’s saving grace has appeared and is offered to all people — supremely in the coming of Jesus Christ.
That grace trains us to say no to ungodliness and worldly desires and to live self-controlled, upright, godly lives now.
Meanwhile we wait for our blessed hope: the glorious appearing of our great God and Savior, Jesus Christ.
He gave Himself for us to free us from all lawlessness and to purify a people who belong especially to Him, eager to do good.

f.g: Buy back, set free by paying a price.
A people for His own special possession.

chapters.n: Teach these things, encourage, and correct with full authority. Don’t let anyone disregard you.
Remind the Saints to respect government and officials, obey the law, and be ready for every good work in the community.
Don’t slander anyone or pick fights. Be gentle and courteous toward everyone.
After all, we too were once foolish, disobedient, misled, slaves to passions and pleasures, living in malice and envy, hated and hating. Remembering our past makes us patient with others.
But then the kindness and love of God our Savior for humanity appeared —

f.w: love of God our Saviour toward man

chapters.n: — and He saved us, not because of good deeds we had done, but out of His mercy, through the cleansing of new birth and the renewing of the Holy Ghost — pointing to baptism and the gift of the Holy Ghost.

f.g: The washing that brings rebirth — baptism.

chapters.n: God poured out the Spirit on us generously through Jesus Christ our Savior.
So that, made right with God by His grace, we would become heirs of eternal life, the very thing we hope for.

f.g: Declared righteous, made right with God.

chapters.n: This is a trustworthy saying. Paul wants Titus to emphasize these truths so believers will devote themselves to good works — grace leads to good works, not away from them.
Avoid foolish debates, speculative genealogies, arguments, and fights about the law of Moses; they are useless and empty.

f.g: Speculative lineages used for fanciful doctrines — different from genuine family history.

chapters.n: Warn a divisive person once, then twice; after that, have nothing more to do with him.

f.g: Greek hairetikos — a divisive, faction-making person.

chapters.n: Such a person is twisted and sinful, condemned by his own conduct.
Paul will send Artemas or Tychicus to take Titus’s place; then Titus should hurry to meet Paul in Nicopolis, where Paul plans to spend the winter.

f.g: Probably the city in western Greece on the Adriatic coast.

chapters.n: Help Zenas the lawyer and Apollos on their journey generously so they lack nothing.

f.g: Possibly an expert in Jewish law or in Roman law.

chapters.n: Our people must learn to devote themselves to good works that meet real needs, so they won’t be unproductive.
Paul sends greetings from everyone with him and asks Titus to greet the believers who love them. Grace be with you all.
